utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, will you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Counsel. For the Prosecution, Chester Stamp and Ekkehard Withopf, with Kimberly Fleming, the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, lead counsel; Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel; and Mirna Milanovic, legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and legal assistant, Nermin Mulalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Chamber wishes to greet all those present, representatives of the Prosecution, the counsel for the accused, the accused, and of course all the other staff present in the courtroom. For today we have two witnesses planned. I understand that there's going to be a request for protective measures for the first witness. Due to that, I'm going to ask the registrar that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then, in open session. Apparently the witness can only come within a quarter of an hour, 20 minutes. Considering this situation, since we can only hear the witness in about a quarter of an hour, we are going to stop now and we'll continue at quarter to 10.00. --- Break taken at 9.31 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then. After interrupting the session in order to give the witness time to come here, I would like to know whether at this stage the witness is ready for the hearing with no protection measures. He did not request any special protection measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the next witness, Mr. Dalibor Adzaip, will not request any protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then. Before we bring in the witness, let me just remind all parties that the protection measures are granted only in virtue of exceptional circumstances. Since this is an open session and the trial is always in open session, this is a selective procedure. And also, we have to have some pedagogical effect for the outside world, and it is important for the witness accounts to be heard outside; however, in some instances due to specific, exceptional circumstances which may cause witnesses to fear for their safety or to fear that their accounts here -- yes -- could bring us closer to the truth, but we still need to grant these special circumstances, the special protection to the witness. So all these request will looked into on a case-by-case basis. And as you have seen, before making any decision in that respect we always listen to the witness and ask them to explain their situation and make their point for themselves, because sometimes there may be differences. I mean, however, we have to make a distinction between two things: We may have eyewitnesses - that's the one thing - but the fears that they may have may be objective or subjective. That's a different problem. We shouldn't confuse the two. And sometimes the very fact that they may be called upon to give their witness account publicly and orally and sometimes, of course, we do grant these protective measures. But even if we do grant these measures, it is still possible for the Defence team to put the questions to the witness in question, so the Defence rights and the rights of the accused are protected, are guaranteed. Having said that, we are now going to call in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then. Good day, sir. First of all, let me check that you can hear what I'm saying in your own language. Can you hear the translation of my words in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then. Sir, you will have to make an oath. But before you do that, you have to tell us your name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dalibor Adzaip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 6th of November, 1974.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were born where? In what town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Travnik, in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your current profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am an electrical technician, an electrician. And at the moment, I'm living in the US.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are in the US. Are you a resident in the US? Do you have a US nationality? What is your situation there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only have the residence and the work permit. I don't have the US citizenship.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And 1993, it was more than ten years ago in fact. What was your professional situation at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the place where I was living and at the time - it depends on the time of the year, in fact - but for a while I was a member of the HVO, and another part of the year --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Fine. That's very good. Now, you are going to read the oath in your own language. Could you please read out this text.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You may sit down now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then. Since you have to testify before the Court, it is my duty to specify a couple of points to you with regard to the way in which this hearing is going to proceed and about what you will have to say. You will have to reply to questions which will be put to you by the representatives of the Prosecution, sitting to your right. It is the person seated to your right. Thereupon, the Defence team for the accused, seated to your left, will also ask you some questions. And the three Judges, sitting in front of you, may intervene at any point, depending on your replies, in order for you to clarify any of the replies you may have given to either the Prosecution or the Defence. Since you have given us the oath that you will speak the truth and only the truth, it means that you can't give us false testimony. If you were to do so anyway, you would be liable for prosecution for that and a possible penalty of up to six years in prison. Since you have given us your oath, you have to say the truth. Please do try and reply to the questions put to you in as a comprehensive and precise and specific way as possible, in order for this Trial Chamber to get a whole idea -- a complete idea of what you yourself have seen. When the Defence asks you questions, reply in the same way, in a comprehensive and specific manner. It is also my duty to inform you that the Rules of Procedure state that whatever you say in the course of your testimony may not be used against you, which means that you can give your witness account with no constraints, no worries at all. In case you come up against a difficulty, a problem in relation to any question, do please share that problem with the Trial Chamber, because that's why we are here, to solve any difficulties. Is that clear, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. I am turning to the Prosecution, and I give you the floor. We have an hour and a half, and we shall have our next break at half past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Adzaip, you informed the Trial Chamber that you were born in Travnik. Can you please also inform the Trial Chamber where you lived in early 1993.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Also in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Between your birth and early 1993, did you also live in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes, throughout that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Adzaip, did there come a time when you joined the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: In June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And which military unit of the HVO did you join in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: In those day, it was called the 1st Independent Company of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber where the 1st Independent Company of the HVO was based.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: It was based in the former JNA centre in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please briefly inform the Trial Chamber what your duties have been at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: My duties were to hold guard duty in town and to secure certain HVO facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Adzaip, the town you are referring to, which town is it?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very well. Did there come a time, Mr. Adzaip, when you noticed foreigners arriving in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes. This happened in 1992, in the summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Adzaip, what sort of foreigners were arriving in the summer 1992 in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: They came from Middle East countries or probably Northern Africa, and this was obvious from the colour of their skin, their appearance, the clothing they wore, and many other elements which indicated that they came from areas outside the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: These foreigners from the areas you just indicated, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And can you please detail what sort of arms they had.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Automatic infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please also inform the Trial Chamber whether these foreigners wore any military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: They did, but some had a mixture of military uniforms and their original clothing. But quite a number of them wore uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Adzaip, where these armed foreigners wearing uniforms were based in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: There were quite a lot of them in the lower part of the city, around the Sarena mosque. And I saw quite a number next to the drugstore in the upper part of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Did there come a time, Mr. Adzaip, when you have been arrested?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And can you please inform the Trial Chamber as to when this happened.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: In June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please tell us who arrested you.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: The Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: How do you know that the ones who arrested you were members of the Armija of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: I knew because they were in uniform and they bore the insignia of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'm now going to show via the Sanction technology the Prosecution Exhibit P4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Adzaip, in front of you on the screen you have a photo board with a number of military insignia. Can you please inform the Trial Chamber which one, if any, was worn by -- was used by the ABiH soldiers who arrested you in June 1993.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Number 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I state for the record that the Witness Adzaip identified the military badge number 12 on Prosecution Exhibit P4 as the one used by the soldiers which arrested him in June 1993 in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Adzaip, in June 1993 your arrest, was it in the beginning, in the middle, or towards the end of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Around the middle of the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: After your arrest, where have you been brought to by the ABiH soldiers who arrested you?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: To the former barracks of the JNA, which was situated in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber for how long you have been detained in the former JNA barracks in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: For 11 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: In the course of the 11 days you were detained in the former JNA barracks in Travnik, have you seen any other detainees?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And can you please inform the Trial Chamber how many of other detainees you have seen in the former JNA barracks in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: The cell that I was in, we were in all about 20 of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The 20 of you, can you please tell us about the ethnic background of the detainees.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: All 20 were Catholics; that is, Croats from the area of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please tell us whether the detainees were soldiers and/or civilians.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: The vast majority were civilians. And out of the 20, there may have been only 3 or 4 military men.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Adzaip, do you know why you have been arrested by members of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Have you ever been told by anybody why you have been arrested?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: In the course of your arrest, have you been interrogated?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Officers, probably, from the information services of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'm now going to show the witness a photograph via Sanction. And since it is a new Prosecution exhibit, there are the nine copies available for distribution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Adzaip, can you please tell us what you can see on the photograph in front of you.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: On this photograph, I can see and recognise the room in which I was detained in Travnik in the former JNA barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Witness Adzaip, you will be provided with a paper copy of this photograph. And would you please date and sign it.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution -- could the Prosecution tell us when this photograph was taken, because we assume it wasn't taken at the time when the witness was detained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's completely correct, Mr. President. The photograph was taken in the year 2002 in the course of the investigation against the two accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Very well. Mr. Registrar, will you give us an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be P54.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P54. Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: You said you were detained for 11 days in June 1993 in the former JNA barracks in Travnik. Have you given any documentation about your release after the 11 days?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And what is this documentation about?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: It is a document I received upon my release indicating that I am being released and that I was free to live and work in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And do you know, Mr. Adzaip, who issued this document?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: It was issued by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And do you know, Mr. Adzaip, who signed this release document?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Mehmet Alagic's name is printed, but as far as I can remember it was actually signed on his behalf by Salko Beba.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'm going to present a document to the witness. Again, the nine copies are available for distribution. The copies are available in both the B/C/S language and the English language. Can the B/C/S copy of the document please be -- can the witness please be provided with the B/C/S version of the document and can it please be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Adzaip, to your right you see a document. Can you please tell us what this document is about.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: It is the document I was given after I was released from detention in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution wishes to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please sign this document and date it with today's date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On both the English and B/C/S version of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can we have an exhibit number for the B/C/S and the English versions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number for the B/C/S version will be P55, and the exhibit number for the English translation will be P55/E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: After your release from the former JNA barracks in Travnik, did you go back to serve within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And can you please inform the Trial Chamber as to why -- as to why not.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: When I was released, Travnik was fully under the control of the BH army, so that I was unable to leave Travnik and go to the area under HVO control.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Did there come a time, Mr. Adzaip, when you have been arrested for a second time?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber about the date when you have been arrested for the second time.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: I was arrested for the second time in October 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And do you recall, Mr. Adzaip, the exact date?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: The 19th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: On the 19th of October, 1993, you were arrested. Can you please inform the Trial Chamber as to where you were arrested.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: In Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please tell us who this time arrested you in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: On that occasion, I was arrested by Muslim forces, the so-called Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And can you please provide us with some details about that arrest.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: I had been visiting a friend, and I was on my way back home. And close to the flat where I lived, I was stopped. They asked me my name. They started pushing me around and beating me. And then they took us in the direction of the underground garages of the Amerikanka building in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The time you have been beaten by the Mujahedin, the Muslim forces who arrested you, what sort of tools, if any, did they use to beat you?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Their hands, their legs, and at times with rifle butts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Adzaip, you were saying that they took "us in the direction of the underground garages of the Amerikanka building in Travnik." Were there any other persons who have been arrested?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: When they took me to those underground garages, they pushed me into a van. They covered me with a blanket, and then I could feel that there was some other men with me in that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: After you were covered with a blanket, Mr. Adzaip, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: We were taken in that same vehicle in a direction that was unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And where were you brought to?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: We were taken -- I really didn't know where or for how long the trip took, but we were taken to a house in a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And what happened to you once you arrived at this house in a village?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: When we arrived at that house, we were taken out of the car with our heads down, and then we were locked up in one of the rooms in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And how many people were locked up in a room in that house?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Together with me, there were five people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And do you recall the name or the names of the other people?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes. I can't remember the name of one person only.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please provide us with the names of the persons you can remember.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Ivo Fisic, Ivan Rajkovic, and Dragan Popovic, and I can't remember the name of the fourth person.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Adzaip, the ethnic background of Ivan Rajkovic and Ivo Fisic?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: They were Croats and Catholics.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And do you also know the ethnic background of Mr. Dragan Popovic?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: He was a Serb Orthodox.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Did you know or did you get to know where this house you and the other ones were detained in, where this house is or was located?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Did there come a time later on when you got to know where this house was located, in which area?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: In the course of my stay in that house, I saw a sticker above the door which said that the house had been blessed, so it must have been owned by a Croat who was a Catholic. And after talking to people to whom I told about this, they suppose it must have been in the area to the north of Guca Gora, Maljine, and Mehurici, where there were some Croat villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And is Guca Gora amongst the villages in that area?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: After you were brought to this house and locked up together with Ivan Rajkovic, Ivo Fisic, Dragan Popovic, and a fourth person, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: In the course of that entire first evening and the day after, we were abused, beaten non-stop, and many other things. And then we were subjected to a kind of interrogation. But for the most part, we were just beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And do you know for what reason, if any, you were beaten?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: I don't know any reason at all. I can't see any reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Adzaip, do you know who beat you?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: All the guards who were taking turns there, they would come in and beat us up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The guards, were they civilians or were they soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: They were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: What sort of soldiers? Of which army?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: The Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Adzaip, you were mentioning that you were beaten the entire first evening and the day after non-stop. Can you please go in some more detail in respect to such beatings.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: We were placed in that rather small room, and from time to time, when the guards were bored or they felt like it, they would come in and they would take turns and they would beat us with whatever they could. And sometimes they would take us out of the room and they would try and hit us so that we could fall to the ground and they could see if they could make us bleed or many other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Were all of the detainees you were mentioning earlier on beaten during the first and the second day in the manner you just described?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And were the members of the Muslim forces who guarded and beat you, were they successful in making you bleed?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: During your detention, is there anything significant that happened in the course of your detention?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber what was so significant that you still recall it today.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Well, on the second or the third morning, early in the morning, the door was opened and all of us, except for Ivan Rajkovic, who was left behind, were taken out. The guards took us out. And when I came out of the house, I noticed that there were quite a few other soldiers there and they led us down a path to a clearing. On both sides of the road, there were armed soldiers all along. When we got to the clearing, there were some more soldiers there. And in the middle of the clearing, they had already dug a hole. And the four of us were standing before that hole, 2 or 3 metres away, and the other soldiers were placed in two rows maybe, on the other side of the hole. A little bit later, one of the guards came and tied our hands behind our backs, and they were -- they were yelling, "Tekbir, Allah-U-Ekber," and then one of them came and got Dragan Popovic, who was the last in our row, he took him and made him stand before the hole. When he was standing there, the same man made him fall. He tripped him up so he fell on the side of the hole. And one of the soldiers, who was standing in front of this entire group which was there, moved in the direction of Dragan and he took out his knife. When he came close to Dragan Popovic, he called Hasan twice. Hasan came from the group of soldiers. He was kneeling. And then he lifted Dragan's chin and he slit his throat with a knife. And then there were more calls "Tekbir," and then Hasan was meant to sever Dragan's head, but he couldn't manage. And then he left, and another one came. He threw the knife into the hole and he cut off Dragan's head. He separated it completely from the body, and he proudly lifted it up. And then they went on shouting. And then he moved slowly in our direction, and he -- he made us kiss the head on the mouth -- on the lips and on the front. And then he walked to the hole. They pushed the body into the hole. And then he threw the head in as well. Afterwards, our hands were untied, and then we were pushed to the hole and we were made to cover it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Adzaip, a number of questions for clarification. You were mentioning that the four of you were placed in front of the hole which was already dug at this point in time. Can you please provide us with the names of the four of you.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Dalibor Adzaip, then we had Ivo Fisic, then somebody else I didn't know. I can't remember his name. And the late Dragan Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: You mentioned that you'd seen a number of soldiers once Mr. Popovic was beheaded. Do you have a recollection as to how many soldiers you have seen?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Altogether, according to my estimate, somewhere between 80 and 100 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And what sort of soldiers were they?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: They were the same soldiers who were keeping us prisoner, the members of the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: When you say "the members of the Muslim forces," are you making reference to the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: No. These were the extremists, the extreme forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And what sort of soldiers are you describing as the extremist forces?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Like the ones who kept us prisoner. Whoever is capable of an act of this sort are extremists. There was no need for anything like that. That's why I called them extremists.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Were Mujahedin amongst these extremists?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Adzaip, you mentioned a certain Hasan who started to sever Mr. Popovic's head from his body. And you mentioned a second person, who finally succeeded to do so. This Hasan and this second person, did they volunteer to do the beheading or have they -- have they been asked by somebody?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Hasan was called by the other guy, who then in the end - and perhaps it was a matter of a ritual or something. And I think Hasan was given the order and the other one probably did it of his own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The one who gave him -- who gave Hasan the order, did you get the impression that this was the person in charge, meaning a commander?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: One can get that impression because in -- during the whole time of that ritual, he was standing before everybody else and he was the one who called Hasan out. So he was the most involved. He was walking around all the time, and one could get the impression that he was some sort of commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: After you covered the hole with the corpse of Dragan Popovic with earth, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: We were taken back to the same house where we had been held before, and Ivan Rajkovic, who was left behind, was still waiting for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Did there come a time, Mr. Adzaip, when Mr. Ivo Fisic and Mr. Ivan Rajkovic were taken away?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Adzaip, do you have a recollection as to when this happened?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: First of all, the fourth guy was taken away first - I can't remember his name - after two days maybe, after this incident. And Rajkovic and Fisic were taken away at some point in November.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Do you have a recollection whether it was in the beginning of November, in the middle, or towards the end of November?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Sometime in the middle of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And what happened to you, obviously left behind?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: I was held there for some more time, and then later on I was also consigned to the regular Armed Forces of the BH.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Do you recall for how long you have been left behind?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Perhaps for another fortnight, maybe 20 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: You were just mentioning, Mr. Adzaip, that you were consigned to the regular armed forces of the BH. Can you please provide us with some more detail as to how this happened.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: In the same way it happened with everyone else: They came into the room, they took me out. And in the same way I was brought there, they took me back to Travnik and they handed me over to the military police of the BH army, which at the time was stationed at the former JNA barracks in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: For clarification, who handed you over to the military police of the BiH army which at that time was stationed at the former JNA barracks in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Those same Muslim forces that held me prisoner in that house. The same people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: What happened to you, Mr. Adzaip, after you have been handed over to the military police of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: I stayed there one night. And afterwards, I was taken to the KP Dom Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber, Mr. Adzaip, for how long you stayed in the KP Dom in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Until the 21st of March, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And on the 21st of March, 1994, have you been released?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Did you get to know, Mr. Adzaip, whether during the time of your detention in Orasac, whether anybody informed any member of the ABiH about the fact that you have been detained?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber, Mr. Adzaip, who informed members of the ABiH about the fact that you have been detained in Orasac.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: My mother, but she basically didn't know where I was being held and what happened to me. But since this certificate, signed by Alagic and Beba, certified that I could live and work freely in Travnik. She went and got in touch with them and asked them to try and find out where I was, what was going on and everything else. She waited for a sign of life, to find out that I was alive and well and where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Adzaip.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, this concludes the examination-in-chief of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have some questions to put to you before I give the floor to the Defence team. First of all, before asking you any questions, just now we were submitted the documents P55/BCS and P55 English version. I have informed the parties that it does not appear to me that the English version is the exact equivalent of the B/C/S translation. I've got four comments to make in this respect. At the very top of the document in B/C/S, we have "OG Bosanska Krajina" [as interpreted] and in the English document, it just says "Operation Group." So in theory, what should have been done because proper translation, no additions there; whereas, the translator seems to have added an extra piece of information which was not necessary in a translation. Just "OG" would have been sufficient. And also, on the 17th of June, 1993, in the B/C/S document there is handwritten reference which I can't identify, but apparently it is "JUI," something like that. Whereas, in the English translation, we see no reference of that. And the third comment: In the B/C/S document, between the signature and the main body of the text, we can see completely illegible references, apart from the reference "BS." And in the English translation, we have no indication of the existence of this paragraph, which should be there but has not been translated into English. And the fourth point: Whoever signs on behalf of Alagic -- well, the signature in the B/C/S document says "Beba," and then we can't identify the name. Whereas, in the English translation, it says "Salko Beba." So the translator apparently specified the first name; whereas in the translation they should simply stick to translating what is in the original. So these are the four points I wanted to make to the translation. Apart from that, when such a document submitted to the Court is translated, the general rule in Roman law - but I suppose it applies to all countries in the world - is that the document which is translated -- well, we have to know who translated it. And it would have been a good idea to have a reference to the name of the translator. Right, then. I have decided to make these points for the transcript. Now, sir, coming back to the witness. You have explained to us that when you were held prisoner in that house by the Muslim forces, you were taken out with Popovic, Fisic, and the third person whose identity you can't provide. How is it possible that having lived through such a terrible experience such as yours you still don't know this person's name? Did you not talk to him? Did he not tell you his name?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes, he did tell me, this person whose name I can't remember. But in the course of all that -- I mean, all that was two or three days later, and then two or three days later he left. And for the most part, I spent my time with Rajkovic and I have him to thank for having remained kind of normal. He was a psychologist at a school. And I am doing my best to forget all this. And after ten years, I've come here to try and recollect all that, because in the meantime I've never talked or thought about this, because I think my life is ahead of me. I was rather young at the time. And even at the time I thought that I had my life ahead of me. And I think the best thing for me to do is to move on and not to dwell on that for the rest of my life.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. When all four of you were taken close to that hole which had been dug, and at that point Popovic was taken -- Dragan Popovic -- why him and why not you? Why was he selected? Ten years later, do you have an explanation for the fact that it was him who was chosen, not you yourself, not the psychologist, not Fisic? Why was he executed? I mean, do you know the reason for that? If you don't know, you simply say "I don't know." Because you must have thought about this. Do you know why it was him and not you?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you don't know. You also said, in reply to a question from the Prosecution, that there was a commander present there, the commander for those 80 or 100 people who were there. You don't know his name? You've never found out who it was?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And was he dressed in the same way as all the others? Did he have any -- the same insignia, or was he the same as everyone else?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: He was dressed in a normal way, and there was nothing to distinguish him from the others apart from the fact that, as I've said before, I thought that he, since he was standing before everybody else and he was kind of organising the whole thing, orchestrating it. I thought he was the commander. But I can't say for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You've explained in reply to a question put to you by the Prosecution that the document that was given to you and your mother had that document. And when you were arrested the second time the document that was given to you in June, when you were released on the 17th of June, in the meantime your parents held onto that document.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And your mother, who was looking for you, because she didn't know where you were, she went to see whom exactly in order to find out about you?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Well, the same people who signed that certificate stating that I was free to live and work freely in Travnik: Salko Beba and Alagic and perhaps one of his colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So she went to see Mr. Salko Beba and Alagic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question: You said that when you were arrested the first time you were interrogated by officers of the information service. What is it that makes you say that they were officers and also that they belonged to the information services or intelligence services?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: I think they belonged to the intelligence service because they are the people who do that, I suppose. And I think they were officers because of the way they looked and the way they were dressed and everything else. I didn't really see any rank insignia on them. But I assume that it couldn't have been an ordinary soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And when he questioned you, what did he want to know? What kind of questions did he put to you? Why were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: That was the time when the conflict started between the HVO and the BH army. And they asked me about everything I knew about the HVO forces around Travnik, where I was, what I had done, and everything else linked to the HVO. They wanted to get information about the arming, the deployment of HVO units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, in relation to the comments you made in respect to the translation, I can provide you with a few explanations. First of all, I actually have the original of the document with me which has been provided yesterday evening for the first time by the Witness Adzaip. Based on my limited knowledge of the B/C/S language - however, I invite the B/C/S speakers on the Defence side to comment on it if they wish to do - the three letters "GOD" do not mean anything else but "anno domini." This is the usual thing which is annexed to any date in the Bosnian Croat or Serbian Croat language. The fourth paragraph, Mr. President, Your Honours, you described as being illegible. There is no fourth paragraph. By the manner Witness Adzaip kept this document - and the witness can confirm this - the fourth paragraph is actually some sort of a mirror of the first paragraph, because the witness kept the document as such and because he kept it for many years as such exactly this thing happened. If Your Honours, Mr. President, wish to provide you with the original, I can certainly do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the best idea would be to show the Defence the original and then the Chamber will have a look at it. So, Madam Usher, will you please show the original to Defence counsel. To the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Prosecution has produced for us the original document. We take note of several material elements: First of all, that this document was stuck together with scotch tape; that after the date there is "GOD" in blue; that the signature is in red; but there is a part what I described as a fourth paragraph, which is in black and "BS" is mentioned. So there's no a priori explanation whether it's a reflection of another document that was printed over this document. And also, in the paragraph above, one can hardly see, and there appears to have been some imprint of another document over this document. The most important thing is that this document consists of eight pieces that were stuck together. So I give back this document to the Prosecution. Very well. We have another 20 minutes for the cross-examination up to the break, so I would now like to give the floor to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Adzaip. I'm Edina Residovic, Defence counsel for General Enver Hadzihasanovic. I am really sorry that you went through such a terrible experience, and the Defence for General Hadzihasanovic has no questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. What about the other Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. In view of the fact that today's testimony does not relate to the counts with which Mr. Kubura is charged, we have no questions for this witness either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I turn back to the Prosecution again to see whether they have any additional questions, since the Defence counsel have not cross-examined this witness at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, may I please, based on the comments you made in respect to the original document, ask one or two questions to the witness to give some explanations? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Adzaip, can you please confirm that you handed over this document personally to me yesterday at about 1900 hours?

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Adzaip, can you please inform the Trial Chamber, if you know, who put the eight pieces of this document together.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: It's not eight parts of the document. This is a document that I carried in my pocket for a while. And because it was folded, the paper was about to tear completely, and so I taped it together. And later on I kept it in a normal file, and that is how I've preserved it to the present day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please confirm that this document is the exact very document you were handed over at the point in time when you were released from the Travnik barracks.

utterances.speaker: DALIBOR ADZAIP
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Adzaip.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Adzaip, your testimony is over, as the Prosecution has asked you all the questions it had for you; the Defence, that could have cross-examined you, didn't. You also answered some questions from the Chamber for the sake of clarification. We thank you for coming, the more so as you testified about very painful events that took place in 1993. We wish you a safe return to the United States, as that is the country you are living in at present. And I'm going to ask Madam Usher to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The agenda for this hearing has been exhausted, since the witnesses planned have been heard. Tomorrow, according to the scheduling, we have one witness, in fact, planned. Will that be the last witness for this week, Mr. Withopf?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's correct. That's the last witness for this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Has this witness arrived? I suppose he has.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Yes, the witness has arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll give you the floor in a minute. Regarding next week, again we have a scheduling from Monday to Friday with several witnesses. There will be one witness a day, except for Wednesday, when we have two witnesses planned which may continue over on to Thursday. So that is the planning for next week. The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. A couple of days ago we received this schedule, according to which there were two witnesses planned for tomorrow. So we don't know which witness will be coming tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the Prosecution help us and clarify this point? I think that the answer is that the witness that we had a moment ago, he was planned to continue tomorrow. That is why there were two witnesses. But Mr. Withopf will give us all the necessary clarifications. Who do we have for tomorrow, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, your interpretation is completely correct. The first name on the list for tomorrow is the very same witness whose testimony we just concluded five minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Is that answer satisfactory? I see. As for the planning for the future, I never give the names because of the possibility that some witnesses may request protective measures. So I will never mention the names of the people who will be testifying. So regarding the measures taken for witnesses will also apply to the Defence when they will be producing their witnesses. Are there any other outstanding matters to address? Let me ask the Prosecution. Can the Prosecution give us any further information regarding the CD-ROMs and their admission?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I can. The technical work has been done. The respective portions of the video footage have been isolated and nine copies containing only such portions will be tendered into evidence tomorrow and will be handed over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you for informing us about this. As you know, there are a few more rulings that are outstanding and will be made very shortly. There is a decision regarding the witnesses pursuant to 92 bis witnesses and a decision will be made very shortly. Then there is also on stand-by a decision regarding the admission of certain facts from three other cases. We are about to take a decision on that. And the response of the Prosecution, which we still don't have - or maybe it is about to be produced; I don't know - anyway, we are awaiting that. So there are two decisions to be rendered. It seems to me to be useful to say that with regard to the testimony collected through Article 92 bis, which was not objected to on the part of the Defence, that it would be appropriate to have admitted into evidence the written statements, which were admitted, and to do that we will take advantage of a shorter sitting at which a testimony has been completed to admit into evidence the statements of 92 bis witnesses. To do that, we will apply the following procedure: It will be sufficient to refer to the statement, the name of the witness, the date when that statement was made, the facts contained in the statement; at which point the registrar will give us an exhibit number. And then the Defence will have the number in their possession. This shouldn't take too long, but it is necessary for us to be able to admit those written statements into evidence. This applies only to written statements which were not challenged in any way. Are there any other observations to be made? If not, I will adjourn the sitting and invite everyone to come back tomorrow for the morning sitting, which will begin as usual at 9.00 a.m. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 5th day of February, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.20 a.m.,
